content_preview.title: Chrome 155 Beta Adds Rust-Based JPEG XL Decoding, Post-Quantum WebCrypto Algorithms and Text Module Imports
content_preview.summary: Chrome 155 entered beta on September 16, 2026 with JPEG XL decoding via a Rust decoder, NIST post-quantum algorithms in WebCrypto, and TC39 text module imports.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Chrome 155 is in beta as of September 16, 2026, according to the [Chrome for Developers beta announcement](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-155-beta). The release bundles image-format, cryptography and JavaScript module changes alongside a set of CSS and web API additions.

## What We Know

### JPEG XL decoding

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact Briefing (391 words, within 300-800) with clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. Headline, summary and lead are all backed by the Chrome 155 beta post.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk (gunzip, tag-stripped text). suspicious_patterns is null for both sources, so nothing to adjudicate. source-0.html.gz (developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-155-beta, 200, published September 16, 2026, author Rachel Andrew) confirms: 'Chrome 155 is in beta as of September 16, 2026'; 'Adds support for decoding JPEG XL ( image/jxl ) images in Blink using jxl-rs , a memory-safe pure Rust decoder' plus ISO/IEC 18181, progressive decoding, wide color gamut, HDR, high bit depth and animation; 'Add support for multiple post-quantum cryptographic algorithms standardized by NIST to the Web Cryptography API: ML-KEM (768, 1024) ML-DSA (44, 65, 87) ChaCha20-Poly1305 X-Wing'; Import Text: 'A TC39 proposal to add module import … with { type: "text" } statements to JavaScript. The import attribute loads text data as a string value'; 'Avoid caching module failures' with manual retry by calling import() again; Digital Credentials issuance (university, government agency, bank); media-playback-while-not-visible; CSS symbols(), margin-trim, text-decoration-skip-spaces, corner shorthands; window-management permission with maximize()/minimize()/restore()/setResizable(); srgb-linear and display-p3-linear PredefinedColorSpace. All verified. source-1.html.gz (github.com/libjxl/jxl-rs, 200) confirms the verbatim quote 'a high-performance, conforming, and memory-safe JPEG XL decoder written in Rust' and 'It is the JPEG XL decoder implementation used in Google Chrome / Chromium and Mozilla Firefox'. The article uses the repo only for that description; it makes no licence or status claim beyond it (the repo also shows BSD-3-Clause and 'not (yet) an official reference implementation', neither of which the article asserts). Both body URLs are in article.sources and vice versa.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinations found. Status framing: the article states beta throughout ('is in beta as of September 16, 2026', 'The beta adds support', 'Beta features can change or be pulled before a stable release') and never says these features have shipped or are stable. No stable release date is asserted; the What We Don't Know section correctly says the post gives none. Flag/default status: the beta post does not say whether JPEG XL decoding is enabled by default or behind a flag, and the article makes no claim either way, which is correct. Overstatement pattern check: no origin-trial, flag or platform-limited qualifier in the source is dropped; the post states the changes apply to the beta channel on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS and Windows 'unless otherwise noted'. Digital Credentials issuance is described in the source with Android/Desktop mechanisms, which the article omits but does not contradict. The algorithm list is reproduced exactly as the source lists it; the source's sentence groups ChaCha20-Poly1305 and X-Wing with the 'NIST-standardized post-quantum' set, and the article mirrors that phrasing as attributed to the post.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive; no sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. The only other recent Chrome release article is 2026-09/29-chrome-154-ships-content-sized-iframes-accessible-scroll-marker-modes-and-text-decoration-inset, a different release (154, reached stable) with no overlap in features (no JPEG XL, WebCrypto or text-module content). No other article covers Chrome 155 or jxl-rs.
concerns: Freshness: the source post is dated September 16, 2026, about three weeks before publication, and describes a beta. The article is explicit about beta status and its date, so readers are not misled, but the stable cut may be imminent and some beta items could change.

Minor nit: the source cites the WebCrypto additions to a WICG draft spec (wicg.github.io/webcrypto-modern-algos); the article does not mention the draft status. Not an overstatement on its own, as the article never calls the algorithms standardized in browsers.
recommendations: Future browser briefings should mention a cited draft-spec status where the source gives one, and say explicitly when a source is silent on flag/default status for a headline feature.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, properly hedged beta briefing; every claim traces to the two cited snapshots and the jxl-rs repo is used only for its self-description and Chrome/Firefox usage. Approved.
